reader.notes: With no LOCALE phrase and no CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION (neither exists at 85) RenderStringValue emits CobolIntrinsics.UpperCase = ToUpperInvariant, the same body at every edition. The mapping of letters outside a-z (y-diaeresis to U+0178, micro sign to Greek capital mu) is implementor latitude; D-CASE-MAPPING documents it for 2002/2023 but states no 1985 reading. Witness g85_f37_01 MATCHes at 85.

refuter.evidence: rf2 (rf2-002) at 85: the 1985 class alphanumeric covers numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited and group items (§1989:A.2.2 AR3), all admitted: UPPER-CASE(ZZ9.99 ' 12.50') -> ' 12.50', UPPER-CASE(XXBXX 'abcd') -> 'ABCD', UPPER-CASE(group 'ab'+99) -> 'AB12'; reference-modified result UPPER-CASE(X)(2:3) -> 'ELL' (§1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR2); nested UPPER-CASE(LOWER-CASE('AbC')) -> 'ABC'; comparison in IF works. Refusals: rf6 '' refused (zero-length literal requires 2014), rf7 N"ab" refused (national literal requires 2002), rf10 numeric literal refused COBOL1627. The reader's beyond-a-z mapping (y-diaeresis -> U+0178, micro -> U+039C, length 3 kept) rests on the computer character set being implementor's; the 1985 text does not define 'lowercase letter' beyond that, so not decisive against. Diagnostics at 85 cite §2023 clauses (presentation only). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.44.4 RV1 'each lowercase letter is replaced by the corresponding uppercase letter'. cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.2 AR3 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or a nonnumeric literal must be specified'; OK §1989:A.2.3 'A numeric function may not be referenced where an integer operand is required'; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR2 'A reference-modifier may be specified only for functions of the category alphanumeric'.
